objective: Give the bounded DeviceRuntime ROS 2 bridge a real process entry point with a bounded, worker-joined shutdown, so the read-only SocketCAN telemetry path can actually be started and stopped instead of only being unit-tested.
decision_supported: The bridge architecture doc calls the read-only boundary implemented, but no process constructed the node, spun the bounded executor or joined the runtime worker; this slice makes that path executable and testable.
acceptance: A console entry point starts the SocketCAN read-only bridge with a bounded executor and fails closed on an invalid configuration or a failed configure/activate.
The entry point takes its recorded domain ID from the initialized ROS context instead of the argument default, so the deployment snapshot cannot disagree with the context rclpy actually created.

Shutdown joins the runtime worker within the configured deadline. A signal that already invalidated the ROS context must not skip the bounded stop, and the process must not exit while the worker is still alive.
The process distinguishes a clean run, an invalid configuration, a failed activation and a teardown that could not join the worker through documented exit codes.
The entry point reports the bounded metrics snapshot so an operator has evidence of drops, backpressure and worker liveness for the run.
Importing workbench.hardware still does not import rclpy, and --help works without any ROS installation.
Tests cover argument validation, the fail-closed paths, the context-domain agreement rule and the worker-joined invariant without requiring a physical CAN device.
The worker-joined invariant is registered as a mutation probe, so replacing the ROS-free bounded shutdown with a ROS lifecycle teardown is detected rather than silently orphaning the CAN worker.
evidence: Focused entry point and bridge test output plus Ruff check/format output
Recorded virtual SocketCAN run showing the process publishing bounded telemetry JSON and exiting with the worker joined
Recorded signal-handling probe showing why the ROS-free bounded shutdown is required once the context is invalid
Mutation gate summary showing the bounded-join probe is CAUGHT by the named entry point tests and the checkout is left byte-identical
required repository test, contract, scenario and context checks
stop_conditions: A public interface/schema, firmware, robot-control or service change is required.
The change would make the bridge a command publisher, service, action server or safety authority.
A second worker, queue or lifecycle owner would be introduced.
The hardware shell would be changed to auto-start a control node without an Owner decision.
A virtual or loopback result would be used as physical CAN, MCU, actuator or hard-real-time evidence.
data_classification: bounded read-only device telemetry, health metadata and deployment configuration; no credentials or device write handles
model_policy: No model output is admitted as a hardware command, lifecycle decision, safety state or physical evidence.
risks_and_fallbacks: Physical CAN, MCU, actuator, PREEMPT_RT and hard-real-time behaviour remain NOT_EXECUTED until validated on real hardware.
